questions.question: How does Nihongo select and transform pitch data across homographs, readings, parts of speech, and proper-noun status?
questions.answer: Nihongo Settings attributes pitch-accent data to CJK Dictionary Institute, supplemented by UniDic. Exact Nihongo matching is not a parity requirement; Settings capture is tracked by issue #90.

questions.question: Which speaker actions use human recordings versus speech synthesis, and what are their voice, fallback, cache, interruption, and replay behaviors?
questions.answer: Selecting Play must produce audible pronunciation. Use a pinned licensed recording when available and Japanese platform Speech Synthesis otherwise; exact Nihongo routing, timing, and interruption behavior are not parity requirements.

questions.question: Which Search-rooted capabilities remain available offline, and how do loading, error, retry, stale-data, reconnect, and provider-fallback states differ?
questions.answer: Lookup must work offline. Exact Nihongo network-failure, stale, retry, and reconnect presentation is not a parity requirement.

questions.question: Are ranking, handwriting candidates, radical candidates, example selection, and OCR grouping repeatable across restored runs?
questions.answer: Exact Nihongo run-to-run variability is not a parity requirement; retain observed runs as reference facts and verify Zenbu with deterministic fixtures.

questions.question: What are the controlled boundary behaviors for partial, reversed-order, extra-stroke, kana, and non-jōyō handwriting?
questions.answer: These extra contrasts may improve future coverage but do not gate the current implementation handoff.
